comparator.sourceNotes: Current2026BEB programme,32module bodies, two charts and currently linked joint guide reviewed17November2026. Exact assessed123EC is111common plus the neutral first two Economics-track taught options AEP21806 and UEC22806. Preserve25documented components168EC; exclude3background choice,12thesis and30genuine open from assessment, plus12unlisted restricted science. No permitted science package, AEP preparation waiver or complete pathway certified. Current programme102/all60firstyear and Assessment1-before11thesis conditions remain. Zero-credit safety obligations retained; old guide is corroboration without current AEP applicability proof.

Research Methods in the Social Sciences

components.note: Example for entry with VWO Mathematics A: functions, equations, differentiation and integration in Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B choose Statistics 1 instead.

components.name: The Economics of Agriculture, Food and Policy
components.note: Selected Economics-track option on agricultural and food-policy instruments, EU agricultural policy, international trade and rural development.

components.name: Spatial and Regional Economics
components.note: Selected Economics-track option on location, distance, firms, households and regional economic activity. The zero-credit Fieldwork Safety course is a mandatory prerequisite. General Safety is also required for new students and carries no credits.

components.name: BSc Thesis Economics and Governance
components.note: Twelve credits include a 1-credit Bachelor Assessment and an 11-credit individual thesis. The assessment, including reflection and a motivated study plan, must be passed before thesis writing. Entry requires at least 102 compulsory or restricted credits, including all first-year credits. Research includes a report, presentation and defence; current chair-specific preparation remains unconfirmed.

components.name: Open Electives
components.note: Thirty credits remain genuinely open for a minor or elective courses after reserving the required science selection.

alternatives.concept: Combine microeconomics, macroeconomics, public and behavioural economics and econometrics with mathematical tools, public institutions and sustainability governance. Actual climate and soil/aquifer inquiry supports analysis of environmental, land and water policy. This is a broader response to the confirmed taught core, without claiming the external science package, thesis preparation or complete degree pathway.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Economics and Governance bachelor. Its two 24-EC thesis tracks, Economics and Governance, are equally formal and neither is named by the target. The Economics track appears first in the current official structure and is selected neutrally, independently of UCR fit.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce economic reasoning about markets, incentives and allocation.
Both cover macroeconomic relationships and international economic exchange.
Both develop intermediate microeconomic analysis of behaviour, markets and incentives.

Both directly analyse government taxing/spending, efficiency, distribution, public goods, externalities and social insurance using economic models and research. WUR gives specific Dutch public-finance and EU detail that is not fully reproduced.
Both develop regression-based empirical analysis for estimating economic relationships and policy effects.

UCR macroeconomics includes growth and is already anchored to the combined macro/trade component. This separately credited WUR course develops Solow/endogenous growth, growth accounting and cross-country empirical analysis; no other selected course is assigned as its distinct counterpart.

Organisational psychology studies power, culture, motivation and teams, but not the defining transaction-cost and economic coordination/incentive theories of this WUR institutional-economics course. Preserve the economic-organisation gap.

UCR microeconomics includes imperfect competition and strategic interaction and is anchored to intermediate microeconomics. No separate selected course teaches this dedicated formal industrial-organisation sequence of firm strategy, market power and competition policy.

Meaningful partial relationship in public institutions, political actors and policy decisions. UCR emphasises comparative democracy, parties, elections and empirical political measurement; WUR focuses public organisations, bureaucracies, public-administration theories/tools and a policy game. Comparative constitutional law adds legal constraints, not a broader public-administration replacement.
Both analyse European Union institutions and policy processes.

Both explicitly teach multidisciplinary/interdisciplinary problem-oriented social inquiry: framing a complex problem, research planning, evidence synthesis, stakeholder/context analysis and written/oral reporting. UCR uses conflict cases, a policy brief/dossier and interdisciplinary podcast; WUR uses multidisciplinary teams, seven selectable societal themes and a proposal-led literature/interview study. This is a specific partial research-process relationship, not full project equivalence.

Other selected economics and sociology courses address inequality and intervention, but no single selected course directly combines this long-run global economic-history inquiry, measurement of income/wealth inequality and historical governance cases. Preserve the distinct component.
Both examine institutions, stakeholders and policy change in complex governance problems.

Public Economics teaches externalities and policy instruments and is anchored to Public Sector Economics; sustainability governance supplies policy applications. No separate selected course is assigned to the full environmental-degradation, multi-scale policy-instrument and economic assessment component. These real partial contributions remain credited at programme level.

Behavioural economics and critical social theory provide related perspectives, but no selected course directly teaches this pluralist comparison of economic schools through sustainable food-system debates. Do not substitute generic sustainability or social theory.

Sustainability governance contains energy cases and stakeholder/policy analysis, and is anchored to governance/policy change. No separate selected course directly implements this integrated advanced energy-market, spatial-distribution and economics/governance transition-analysis project.

No selected course directly teaches the EU Common Agricultural Policy, agricultural-trade instruments and AGRIPOL food-market/welfare simulation. General public economics, trade or soil science are substantive complements, not this specific agricultural-policy formation.

No selected course directly develops the economic location/agglomeration and spatial firm/household analysis of this component. Natural-domain soil/aquifer inquiry and regional policy cases do not substitute for spatial and regional economics.
Both provide social-science research design and statistical foundations.

Both develop statistical estimation, hypothesis testing and uncertainty. UCR emphasises mathematical probability/inference and Monte Carlo methods; WUR emphasises applied regression, categorical data, ANOVA/designs and R, so the full applied sequence differs.
Both develop linear-algebra methods used in quantitative analysis.

Research Methods & Statistics is anchored to the broader research-methods component and includes relevant tests/regression. This distinct WUR3ECStatistics2 component remains separate rather than duplicating that one UCRcourse row.

audience.programmeDescription: Economics and Governance studies how markets, institutions and public policy shape sustainability. Economic theory, quantitative research and public administration are applied to food systems, environmental resources, development and energy transitions.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This qualified comparison assesses 123 EC of confirmed taught study: 111 EC common Economics and Governance plus the two illustrated Economics-track courses. The UCR programmes combine substantial economics and research methods with different quantitative, institutional and sustainability priorities. They do not reproduce all specialist agricultural, food, spatial, industrial or energy-transition economics. The required science package, background choice, thesis preparation, final research and complete progression are excluded.

curriculum.limitation: The degree requires 180 EC. All 25 supported components/168 EC remain visible, including 30 EC genuine open study without selected contents. The permitted science package and current AEP-specific thesis preparation remain unverified; this is not a certified complete pathway.

componentNotes.beb-stat2: Develops confidence intervals, tests of means, simple linear regression and correlation, checking model assumptions and good statistical practice.
componentNotes.beb-history: Studies long-run income and wealth inequality, market failures and government intervention, with economic-policy examples and information-literacy work.
componentNotes.beb-economics: Introduces economic models, strategic interaction, limited information, preferences and empirical evidence for understanding inequality and sustainability.
componentNotes.beb-public-admin: Studies public institutions, bureaucracies, policy making and the roles of government, companies and citizens in addressing societal problems.
componentNotes.beb-methods: Develops research objectives, questions and a feasible proposal using experimental, cross-sectional or case-study designs.
componentNotes.beb-macro-trade: Studies the open economy, inflation, unemployment, exchange rates, international trade and the effects of economic and trade-policy instruments.
componentNotes.beb-env-econ: Uses economics to analyse environmental degradation and the effectiveness and efficiency of policy instruments at local through global scales.
componentNotes.beb-food-systems: Compares economic schools of thought on food-system questions involving sustainability, social justice, power, workers and consumers.
componentNotes.beb-adv-stat: Studies regression, analysis of variance, categorical data, non-parametric tests and statistical designs, including analysis and interpretation using R.
componentNotes.beb-problem: Uses multidisciplinary problem-oriented study: an ethical research proposal, a literature or interview-based investigation, and written and oral reporting.
componentNotes.beb-econometrics: Combines economic theory, data and statistical estimation and testing to investigate relationships and answer social-science research questions.
componentNotes.beb-eu: Studies EU institutions, legal frameworks and policy processes, including political struggles over life-science and sustainability issues.
componentNotes.beb-micro: Develops mathematical and graphical models of consumers, producers, markets, uncertainty, asymmetric information and government-policy effects.
componentNotes.beb-growth: Uses growth models and empirical evidence to study differences in income, productivity, technology, institutions and economic development.
componentNotes.beb-linear: Applies vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, iteration, projection and regression, including numerical software.
componentNotes.beb-change: Studies problem definition, agenda setting, decisions, implementation and evaluation as governance arrangements and policy change.
componentNotes.beb-inst-econ: Uses contemporary cases such as land tenure, futures markets and food supply chains to study institutions, incentives and economic organisation.
componentNotes.beb-public-sector: Studies government taxing and spending, efficiency and distribution, behavioural responses, public debt, social security and links with the EU.
componentNotes.beb-energy: Integrates economics and governance to analyse energy markets, externalities, distribution, stakeholder choices and policy interventions in energy transitions.
componentNotes.beb-industrial: Uses formal economic analysis of firm strategies, competition, market power and the role of public policy.
componentNotes.beb-math-choice: Example for entry with VWO Mathematics A: functions, equations, differentiation and integration in Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B choose Statistics 1 instead. This component is outside the assessed 123 EC taught core.
componentNotes.beb-agri-food: Selected Economics-track option on agricultural and food-policy instruments, EU agricultural policy, international trade and rural development.
componentNotes.beb-regional: Selected Economics-track option on location, distance, firms, households and regional economic activity. The zero-credit Fieldwork Safety course is a mandatory prerequisite. General Safety is also required for new students and carries no credits.
componentNotes.beb-thesis: Twelve credits include a 1-credit Bachelor Assessment and an 11-credit individual thesis. The assessment, including reflection and a motivated study plan, must be passed before thesis writing. Entry requires at least 102 compulsory or restricted credits, including all first-year credits. Research includes a report, presentation and defence; current chair-specific preparation remains unconfirmed. This component is outside the assessed 123 EC taught core.
componentNotes.beb-electives: Thirty credits remain genuinely open for a minor or elective courses after reserving the required science selection. This component is outside the assessed 123 EC taught core.
